symbols.description: Organization cited as stating the proportions of congestion attributable to bottlenecks and poor signal timing.
symbols.name: FHWA

symbols.description: Corridor coalition associated with the congestion study said to underlie the frequently quoted proportions.
symbols.name: I-95 Corridor Coalition

symbols.description: Traffic condition discussed as having recurring and nonrecurring causes and as occurring either locally or systemically.
symbols.name: congestion

symbols.description: Congestion attributed to recurring causes, especially bottlenecks and poor signal timing.
symbols.name: recurring congestion

symbols.description: Congestion other than recurring congestion, including congestion associated with special events, bad weather, work zones, and traffic incidents.
symbols.name: nonrecurring congestion

symbols.description: A specific location or point associated with localized traffic congestion, upstream queue formation, and free-flowing traffic downstream.
symbols.name: bottleneck

symbols.description: A recurring cause of congestion identified as a tangible problem rather than a random event.
symbols.name: poor signal timing

symbols.description: A cause associated with a bottleneck, including physical roadway deficiencies and other conditions such as weaving, sun glare, rubbernecking, or a vertical climb.
symbols.name: bottleneck cause

symbols.description: A physical roadway condition that can cause a bottleneck, such as a lane drop or other operationally deficient roadway design.
symbols.name: physical bottleneck cause

symbols.description: An operational deficiency in roadway design that can contribute to a recurring bottleneck.
symbols.name: roadway design deficiency

symbols.description: A roadway design condition given as an example of a physical bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: lane drop

symbols.description: A roadway traffic condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: weaving condition

symbols.description: An environmental condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: sun glare

symbols.description: A traffic-related condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: rubbernecking

symbols.description: A roadway condition given as an example of a bottleneck cause.
symbols.name: vertical climb

symbols.description: An example of a nonrecurring congestion event.
symbols.name: special event

symbols.description: An example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: bad weather

symbols.description: An example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: work zone

symbols.description: An example of a nonrecurring congestion cause.
symbols.name: traffic incident

symbols.description: A line of vehicles formed upstream of a bottleneck.
symbols.name: queue

symbols.description: The direction or region before a bottleneck where queues form and traffic may propagate.
symbols.name: upstream

symbols.description: The direction or region after a bottleneck where traffic is described as free-flowing or where a downstream front may be fixed or moving.
symbols.name: downstream

symbols.description: Traffic moving without the localized or systemic congestion described for the other traffic phases.
symbols.name: free-flowing traffic

symbols.description: A traffic phase involving localized congestion in Kerner's three-phase categorization.
symbols.name: synchronized flow

symbols.description: A traffic phase characterized as more or less systemic congestion, with downstream traffic velocity moving while traffic may propagate upstream through bottlenecks.
symbols.name: wide-moving jam

symbols.description: One of the three categories in Kerner's traffic categorization: free-flow, synchronized flow, or wide-moving jams.
symbols.name: traffic phase

symbols.description: A front at which Kerner's synchronized traffic is described as fixed; it is characterized as a de facto bottleneck.
symbols.name: downstream front

symbols.description: The amount of traffic using or attempting to use a roadway, which can overwhelm available roadway capacity.
symbols.name: traffic demand

symbols.description: The available capacity of a roadway that may be overwhelmed by traffic demand.
symbols.name: roadway capacity

symbols.description: Delay that occurs when a recurring bottleneck's design deficiency combines with traffic overburden.
symbols.name: traffic delay

symbols.description: Traffic demand exceeding or overwhelming available roadway capacity in the context of a recurring bottleneck.
symbols.name: traffic overburden

symbols.description: The velocity of traffic downstream, described as moving in wide-moving jams.
symbols.name: downstream traffic velocity

symbols.description: Movement of traffic upstream through bottlenecks, particularly in the description of wide-moving jams.
symbols.name: traffic propagation

symbols.description: Formation of queues upstream of a bottleneck.
symbols.name: queue formation

symbols.description: A study said to have been undertaken mostly for, or using data mostly from, the I-95 Corridor Coalition and used as the primary basis for the quoted congestion proportions.
symbols.name: congestion study

symbols.description: The quoted proportion of congestion attributed jointly to bottlenecks and poor signal timing, stated as 45 percent.
symbols.name: recurring congestion proportion

symbols.description: The quoted proportion of nationwide congestion attributed to bottlenecks, stated as 40 percent.
symbols.name: bottleneck congestion proportion

symbols.description: The quoted proportion of nationwide congestion attributed to poor signal timing, stated as 5 percent.
symbols.name: poor-signal-timing congestion proportion
